newsitem.title: UK: Princess Di consults UK ministers on landmines.
newsitem.headline: Princess Di consults UK ministers on landmines.

text.p: Princess Diana was briefed by British ministers on Wednesday ahead of a U.S. fund-raising gala for mine victims, but officials stressed she would not be acting on behalf of the government.
Diana, who has taken a high-profile interest in the victims of anti-personnel mines, talked for 30 minutes with Foreign Secretary Robin Cook and Overseas Development Minister Clare Short.

Officials said they had briefed Diana on their attempts to ban the use of mines. She is due to attend a June 17 fund-raising dinner in Washington organised by the U.S. Red Cross to help landmine victims.
"The princess called on the two ministers at her own request to discuss her visit to the United States," a foreign office spokesman said.
"There is no question of the princess acting for the government. Visits of this kind are undertaken in a private capacity."
Diana, who was divorced from Prince Charles last year, has raised hackles in the British establishment by suggesting she could help represent the country abroad as a roaming ambassador-at-large.
Last month the new Labour government promised to destroy all Britain's anti-personnel mines by 2005, pursuing its pledge to put human rights at the centre of foreign policy.

Cook stresses the need for action on mines, blamed for killing 25,000 people a year and maiming many more. The Red Cross estimates there are 120 million mines in the ground across the world, many of them in poor, war-torn countries like Angola and Cambodia.
In February Diana issued a heartfelt plea for an immediate worldwide ban on mines after a visit to Angola, where she saw children who had been injured after accidentally detonating the devices.
